title: Cofiltered coherent diagrams whose arrows are equivalences
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty ordinary category such that any two objects receive arrows from a common object and every parallel pair $f,g:i\to j$ is equalized by some arrow $k\to i$. Let $\mathscr C$ be an enhanced category in the larger universe (a category retaining mapping spaces and all composition homotopies, equivalently an infinity category). A coherent diagram on $I$ consists of its objects, arrows, composition homotopies for strings of arrows and all higher compatibilities, i.e. a functor from the nerve $N(I)$ to $\mathscr C$. Write $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(N(I),\mathscr C)$ for the full enhanced subcategory of diagrams sending every arrow of $I$ to an equivalence. Then the constant-diagram functor
$$\mathscr C\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(N(I),\mathscr C)$$
is an equivalence; evaluation at any fixed object of $I$ is an inverse equivalence. For each such diagram $F$, its homotopy limit exists and every projection $\operatorname{holim}_I F\to F(i)$ is an equivalence. The space of limiting cones is contractible. These constructions are natural for coherent transformations of diagrams and for changes of indexing category between nonempty cofiltered categories. The same assertions hold for filtered categories and homotopy colimits. They apply also when $\mathscr C$ is an enhanced functor category, so that the cones and equivalences are natural in its parameters. No assertion is made about diagrams having noninvertible arrows or about the empty index category.
